name: Learn: AppArmor Confinement
description: Confine containers with AppArmor step by step — write and load a profile on a node with apparmor_parser, reference it from a pod via securityContext.appArmorProfile, verify a denied action is blocked, and contrast confined vs unconfined pods. Exam-focused runtime-security practice.
objective: CKS › System Hardening (15%). Goal: write and load an AppArmor profile on a node, reference it from a pod (localhost/<name>), prove a denied operation is blocked, and contrast confined vs unconfined workloads — the mandatory-access-control hardening the exam expects.

questions.title: Load an AppArmor profile on a node
questions.teach:
**AppArmor** is a Linux Security Module giving path-based **Mandatory Access Control**. A profile names a program and lists rules; `deny /etc/secret-data/** w,` blocks writes under that path. Load it on the node with `apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/<file>` (`-W` waits).

**Gotcha:** the kernel tracks a profile by its **profile name** (the string after the `profile` keyword), not the filename — a pod references that name, so keep them matching.
questions.prompt:
On worker node `$W1`, create an AppArmor profile file at `/etc/apparmor.d/k8s-deny-write` with profile name `k8s-deny-write` that **denies all writes** to files under `/etc/secret-data/`, then load it with `apparmor_parser`.

Target: the file `/etc/apparmor.d/k8s-deny-write` exists on `$W1` and contains a `deny` write rule for `/etc/secret-data/`.
questions.hint:
Use a heredoc through `docker exec -i "$W1" tee /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-deny-write`. The profile body: `#include <tunables/global>` then `profile k8s-deny-write flags=(attach_disconnected) { #include <abstractions/base>
  file,
  deny /etc/secret-data/** w,
}`. Load with `docker exec "$W1" apparmor_parser -r -W /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-deny-write`.

verification.description: profile /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-deny-write with a deny-write rule exists on $W1

questions.title: Reference the profile from a pod
questions.teach:
A container requests a profile via `securityContext.appArmorProfile` (GA in 1.30+). Use `type: Localhost` with `localhostProfile: k8s-deny-write` to apply a profile already loaded on the node — the value is the **profile name**, not a file path.

**Gotcha:** `Localhost` only works if that profile is loaded on the node the pod lands on — here we pin with `nodeName: $W1`. If it's missing, the pod won't start.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-apparmor`, create a pod `confined` pinned to node `$W1`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`, whose container `hello` references the **localhost** AppArmor profile `k8s-deny-write`.

Target: pod `confined` is on `$W1` and its container requests the localhost profile `k8s-deny-write` (via `appArmorProfile` or the beta annotation).
questions.hint: Set `spec.containers[0].securityContext.appArmorProfile: { type: Localhost, localhostProfile: k8s-deny-write }` and `spec.nodeName: $W1`. (Equivalent annotation: `container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/hello: localhost/k8s-deny-write`.)
questions.solution:
cat <<YAML | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: confined
  namespace: cks-apparmor
spec:
  nodeName: $W1
  containers:
  - name: hello
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      appArmorProfile:
        type: Localhost
        localhostProfile: k8s-deny-write
YAML

verification.description: pod 'confined' on $W1 references localhost profile k8s-deny-write

questions.title: Verify the confinement blocks a write
questions.teach:
On an AppArmor-capable node the enforce-mode profile actually **blocks** the denied action. Prove it: `kubectl exec confined -- sh -c 'touch /etc/secret-data/x'` returns `Permission denied` on a real host. (This Mac has no AppArmor, so it would succeed — hence requires-host.)

**Gotcha:** the rule is path-based — test the **protected** path, not `/tmp` (which the profile allows), or you'll see no denial.
questions.prompt:
Run a write to the **protected** path inside the `confined` pod (`touch /etc/secret-data/x`) and capture its output into a ConfigMap `apparmor-proof` (key `result`) in `cks-apparmor`.

Target: ConfigMap `apparmor-proof` exists and its `result` shows the write was denied (contains `Permission denied`).
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-apparmor create configmap apparmor-proof --from-literal=result="$(kubectl -n cks-apparmor exec confined -- sh -c 'touch /etc/secret-data/x' 2>&1)"` — write to a path the profile denies (`/etc/secret-data/`), not `/tmp` (which the profile allows).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n cks-apparmor create configmap apparmor-proof \
  --from-literal=result="$(kubectl -n cks-apparmor exec confined -- sh -c 'touch /etc/secret-data/x' 2>&1)"
# on an AppArmor host the result is: touch: /etc/secret-data/x: Permission denied

verification.description: confined container still bound to profile k8s-deny-write (enforcement needs host)

questions.title: Contrast: unconfined vs confined
questions.teach:
To see what AppArmor buys you, compare two pods. A container with **no** `appArmorProfile` (or `type: Unconfined`) runs unconfined — the write to `/etc/secret-data/` succeeds, while the `confined` pod blocks it. Confinement is deliberate and per-container. **Gotcha:** `kubectl get pod

-o yaml | grep -i apparmor` catches both the typed field and the beta annotation — an empty jsonpath on the typed field alone is ambiguous.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-apparmor`, create a second pod `unconfined` on node `$W1`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`, with **no** AppArmor localhost profile (leave it unset, or set `type: Unconfined`).

Target: `unconfined` does NOT reference `k8s-deny-write`, while `confined` (Step 2) still does — the two pods differ in their AppArmor setting.
questions.hint: Just omit the `appArmorProfile`/annotation on `unconfined` (or set `appArmorProfile.type: Unconfined`). The validator confirms `confined` has the localhost profile and `unconfined` does not.
questions.solution:
cat <<YAML | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unconfined
  namespace: cks-apparmor
spec:
  nodeName: $W1
  containers:
  - name: hello
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML
# Compare:
kubectl -n cks-apparmor get pod confined   -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].securityContext.appArmorProfile}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n cks-apparmor get pod unconfined -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].securityContext.appArmorProfile}{"\n"}'

verification.description: confined uses k8s-deny-write; unconfined does not (the two differ)
